ai.title: Add --agent and --params CLI flags for explicit agent selection
ai.summary: Added `--agent <id>` and `--params <json>` flags to the CLI to bypass cost-mode mapping and invoke specific agents. Backend `main-prompt.ts` validates agent IDs against `agentRegistry` and prioritizes explicit selection over default templates. `npm-app` parses JSON params, passing them via `promptParams` in the client action schema. Updated `cli-definitions.ts`, `types.ts`, and help text to support the new options.

eli5.text: If you run the tool from the command line, you can now tell it exactly which assistant to wake up instead of letting it guess based on how much you're willing to spend. Two new options, --agent to name the assistant (like "reviewer" or "thinker") and --params to hand it extra settings as text, override the usual pick-by-price behavior, and the tool will refuse to start if you name an assistant that doesn't exist. It's already live today for anyone typing commands into the terminal.

ai.title: Add print mode flag to CLI
ai.summary: Introduced `--print` (`-p`) flag to `codebuff` CLI enabling non-interactive execution. Runs until first response completes then exits, requiring prompt or `--params`. Greeting and interactive setup skipped; unauthenticated print mode exits with error. Affects `npm-app/src/cli-definitions.ts`, `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, `npm-app/src/index.ts`, `npm-app/src/types.ts`.

eli5.text: You can now run the assistant in a non-interactive mode by adding a new command-line flag (such as `-p` or `--print`). When you use this flag, the assistant will start, generate its response, and then exit automatically without waiting for you to keep chatting. This mode skips the usual welcome message and interactive setup, and if you are not logged in, the assistant will simply stop with an error instead of asking you to sign in. The change is live today for anyone running the tool from the command line.

ai.title: CLI cwd flag replaces positional argument
ai.summary: Project directory selection moved from positional argument to --cwd flag in npm-app/src/cli-definitions.ts and index.ts. Breaking change for scripts passing path as first arg; now requires explicit flag. Scope: CLI interface, types.ts CliOptions, package.json start scripts.

eli5.text: When you tell the tool which folder to work in, you now have to use the phrase --cwd followed by the folder name, instead of just typing the folder name on its own. Scripts or shortcuts that used the old way (typing the path as the very first thing) must switch to the new format, otherwise they will no longer find the right folder. If you watched someone run the tool, you'd notice the command line now shows --cwd before the folder path, and the list of available options now spells out --cwd as a named choice instead of treating the first word as the folder.

ai.title: Add / command to menu and fix help prompt
ai.summary: The CLI menu now displays "/" as a command to list available commands. The startup prompt was updated to suggest "/help" instead of "help". Leading whitespace was removed from the ASCII art banner in `npm-app/src/menu.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts up, the welcome message now tells you to type /help instead of just help if you want to see the list of commands. The menu that shows your available commands now also lists / at the top, so you can type / to see that same list at any time. The startup banner graphic also had a small blank line removed from its beginning. These tweaks are live today and only affect how the commands are presented to you.

ai.title: Remove GITHUBTOKEN log from release script
ai.summary: Deleted console.log notification for GITHUB_TOKEN usage in `httpGet`. Prevents token presence from being printed to stdout during releases. Affects `npm-app/release/index.js`. No functional change to authentication headers.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes release step that builds and ships your software used to print a line saying it was using your GitHub login token while running. That line has been removed, so releasing software no longer leaves that token-notification text in the build output. Nothing about the login itself changed, so your access and authentication stay exactly as they were.

ai.title: Refactor tool handlers to unified format and remove WIP tool
ai.summary: Removed `WIP_TOOLS` constant and `NonWIPTool` type from `backend/src/tools/constants.ts` to unify tool handler signatures. Handlers for `spawn_agents`, `think_deeply`, `update_report`, and `web_search` are now registered in `codebuffToolHandlers` alongside existing tools. State access in handlers like `add-subgoal.ts` migrated to `state.mutableState.agentContext`, and `run-tool.ts` initializes `agentContext` as an object. `parseRawToolCall` in `tools.ts` now preserves `rawToolCall.toolCallId` instead of generating new IDs on error.

eli5.text: The assistant's specialized tools, like spawning helper agents, deep reasoning, updating reports, and web searches, have been rewired into the main tool system instead of running through a separate test setup. You won't see a new feature, but if you watched how tools are loaded, you'd notice they're now registered uniformly alongside the older tools rather than being flagged as experimental. The internal tracking of conversations and tool IDs has also been tidied up so tool results link back to the correct request instead of generating new IDs mid-processing.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.432
ai.summary: Patch release 1.0.432 for codebuff. Version updated in npm-app/release/package.json.

eli5.text: Updating to version 1.0.432 lets you start the assistant from a specific project folder using the new --cwd option instead of the old way, and you can now run it once without interactive prompts using --print. A new --agent flag lets you pick exactly which assistant profile to use, and the menu now shows "/" as a shortcut to see all available commands. The release also trims chat history slightly to stay within the new token limit. These changes are live today for anyone using the latest version.

ai.title: dev.sh passes explicit --cwd flag to bun start-bin
ai.summary: scripts/dev.sh now passes the `--cwd` flag to `bun start-bin` instead of relying on positional argument interpretation. This ensures the client starts in the correct directory context during local development. The change affects only the `scripts/dev.sh` file within the Tooling area.

eli5.text: You probably didn't notice, but the local development helper for contributors has gotten slightly more reliable. When someone runs the tool that boots up the app for testing locally, it now explicitly tells the program which folder to start in, instead of guessing based on position. This avoids confusion in edge cases where the working directory wasn't set correctly. The change is internal, affects only the developer experience, and doesn't change any features or behavior for end users.

ai.title: Add debug logging for tool calls and results in stream-parser
ai.summary: Stream parser logging for tool calls and results downgraded from info to debug level. Tool call detection and result processing now include toolCallId in the log message for better traceability. Affects backend/src/tools/stream-parser.ts.

eli5.text: The system now records more detailed behind-the-scenes notes about when it asks for a tool to do something and gets an answer back, and those notes now also include the ID of that tool so they can be traced together later. Previously these notes were written at a basic level that was always visible; they are now written at a quieter debug level, so they only show up when someone is specifically looking for them during troubleshooting. This affects only the internal stream processing used by the assistant backend and has no impact on what you see or experience directly.

ai.title: findfiles tool handler mutableState migration
ai.summary: handleFindFiles migrates from direct state.messages access to state.mutableState.messages. Root cause: state schema refactor isolating mutable fields. Affects backend/src/tools/handlers/find-files.ts. Optional chaining on mutableState prevents runtime crash if field absent.

eli5.text: The internal tool that searches for files no longer crashes when it can't find the message history it needs. Instead of looking directly inside the session's stored data, the tool now checks a separate, safer location that was designed for information that changes frequently. You won't see a new button or feature; this just keeps the file search running smoothly behind the scenes. The small adjustment is already live in the service today.

ai.title: Refactor tool handler inputs
ai.summary: Tool handler signatures in `backend/src/tools/handlers/` now accept `agentStepId`, `clientSessionId`, and `userInputId` as top-level parameters instead of reading them from `state`. `backend/src/tools/constants.ts` updated `CodebuffToolHandlerFunction` type to reflect this change. `backend/src/tools/stream-parser.ts` removed these fields from the state object construction. `write-file.ts` switched `agentMessagesUntruncated` source to `mutableState.messages`.

eli5.text: When the assistant calls on internal tools like reading a file or looking up documentation, it used to dig the tracking numbers out of a shared state object, where they might be missing and cause an error. Now those tracking numbers are handed to each tool directly as explicit inputs, and the shared state no longer carries them, so the tools are fed what they need up front instead of having to reach for it and hope it is there. This is live today as behind-the-scenes housekeeping: you should notice nothing from the outside, but the assistant's internal tool calls are a little more robust and predictable.
